scenarios.name: ci-deploy-with-project-token
scenarios.rationale: Both use a project token as RAILWAY_TOKEN, pass --service, avoid `railway deploy`, and don't need an interactive login; B uses `--ci` in the actual command, and also mentions `--detach`, while A uses `--detach` in the command and mentions `--ci` as an alternative, but A wrongly claims `--ci` streams until build completion in a way that is fine yet also A is a bit more verbose; B adds a reference to a nonexistent 'Task H' which is a minor flaw.

scenarios.name: postgres-add-and-migrate
scenarios.rationale: B matches the rubric closely: `railway add --database postgres`, `railway variable set ... --service`, `railway run --service orders-api -- npx prisma migrate deploy` with flags before `--`, and the note that `railway run` runs locally against a private `*.railway.internal` host with a pre-deploy command as the alternative; A uses `railway variables --set` and never runs the required migration command for orders-api, only running it via `--service Postgres` with the public URL or a pre-deploy command, though it does cover the local/internal-host caveat.

scenarios.name: rollback-and-secret-safe-variable
scenarios.rationale: A states there is no rollback command, rejects `railway down` and `railway redeploy`, gives the dashboard and `git checkout` plus `railway up` routes, and uses the exact `echo "$STRIPE_SECRET" | railway variable set STRIPE_SECRET_KEY --stdin --skip-deploys`; B hedges on the CLI having no rollback command, recommends a dashboard 'Rollback' button, and uses `--set` with the expanded value instead of the `--stdin` pipe.
